$comment: Labelled evaluation set for review analysis (P1a-T3).
Forty reviews, twenty Turkish and twenty English, matched in difficulty so
the two languages can be compared honestly — the point of the set is to show
whether Turkish quality holds up against English, and that only means
something if both halves contain the same mix of easy and hard cases.
Each half has 7 positive, 6 negative and 7 neutral, deliberately: an
unbalanced set makes accuracy look good for the wrong reason (always guess
the majority class), which is why the script reports macro-F1 too.
`hard` marks the cases where a human might reasonably disagree — sarcasm,
faint praise, mixed reports. They are scored like any other, but reported
separately so a regression in the easy cases cannot hide behind them.
`themes` lists words we expect to see reflected in the topics. Matching is
substring-based and any-of, not exact: the model chooses its own wording and
grading it on vocabulary rather than comprehension would measure nothing.
